cues: Chlorobenzene has no positional isomer, since all six ring carbons are equivalent.
Isomerism starts with a second substituent: dichlorobenzene has exactly three, ortho, meta and para.
Their boiling points are close, but para melts at plus fifty three degrees while the others melt far below zero.
Its symmetrical shape stacks neatly in the crystal, so more energy is needed to break the lattice.
